chunks: PCB layers and their materials. The question: What are the layers of a PCB? What are they made of?
A circuit board is a flat sandwich of thin copper sheets and insulating layers, pressed together into one solid piece.
The copper carries current, the insulation keeps the copper layers apart, and coatings on the outside protect it and label it.
Knowing what each layer is made of lets you predict how the board behaves.
Think of a layered sandwich. Thin slices of cheese (copper) sit between slabs of bread (the insulating layers). The bread is glass cloth soaked in epoxy glue.
Some slabs come already baked hard, and others are a sticky spread that melts in the oven and glues the sandwich together.
A glossy glaze on top (soldermask) and writing in icing (silkscreen) finish it.
The analogy is loose on one point: the copper is etched into tracks and shapes, not left as full slices.
A 4-layer board cross-section (thicknesses not to scale). The three dielectric layers (two prepregs and a core) separate four copper layers.
Soldermask and silkscreen cover the outside; a plated via barrel connects layers.
The thick core gives mechanical stiffness; the thin prepregs set the spacing between outer signal layers and the inner planes, which sets controlled impedance.
Core: a rigid, fully hardened sheet of glass and epoxy with copper on one or both faces. Prepreg: glass cloth with partly hardened epoxy.
It melts under heat and pressure and glues layers together. Ounce (oz) of copper: a foil weight. 1 oz is about 0. 035 mm thick ("Best conductor material for PCB layers").
Soldermask: the green coating that covers copper except at the pads, where parts are soldered ("What soldermask is and does").
Silkscreen: the white ink text and symbols printed on top ("The silkscreen (legend) layer"). Surface finish: a thin coating on exposed pads that keeps them easy to solder.
Stack a common 4-layer board from the top down. Top copper is 0. 035 mm and prepreg is 0. 2 mm. The inner copper is 0. 0175 mm and the core is 1. 0 mm. Then come another 0.
0175 mm of inner copper, 0. 2 mm of prepreg and 0. 035 mm of bottom copper. These add up to 1. 505 mm. Two soldermask coats of 0. 025 mm add 0. 05 mm, giving 1.
555 mm, which is the ordinary 1. 6 mm board. That is the whole idea.
"A rigid PCB is copper foil layers on FR-4, which is fibreglass cloth in epoxy.
Multilayer boards are built from cores, which are cured laminate with copper on both sides, and prepreg, partly cured glass-epoxy that bonds the layers under heat and pressure.
Outside, there's soldermask, a green epoxy coating that covers everything but the pads, silkscreen ink for labels, and a surface finish such as ENIG or HASL on the pads.
Vias are plated holes connecting the layers. A typical 1. 6 millimetre four-layer board has 35 micron outer copper and 0. 2 millimetre prepreg."
